root_idea.summary: The root centers on loss, diminution, and deficiency—the opposite of increase.
root_idea.development: Its semantic range develops from a thing losing part or becoming less to causing reduction, shortfall, or impairment in something due; related nouns denote the loss itself, a defect, or the amount lost.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form نَقَصَ.
Displayed as the passive participle citation form مَنْقُوصٌ.
Displayed as the verbal noun نَقْصٌ.

senses.definition: To become less or deficient; or to reduce, curtail, or take away part of something.
senses.usage_conditions: Covers ordinary diminution of an amount, measure, extent, lifespan, or remaining portion. Quranic usage includes active transitive reduction and passive being diminished; grammatical voice and aspect do not create separate senses.

senses.definition: To diminish or withhold something from a person; to fail someone in something owed or expected.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a person as the affected party and the diminished thing as the object. In the Quranic construction of 9:4, it means not failing the addressees in anything.

senses.definition: Diminished, reduced, or made deficient through the loss of part.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it describes an allotted share or due that is not reduced or withheld.

senses.definition: Loss, diminution, or shortfall in an amount, share, possession, or state of completeness.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it denotes loss from wealth and lives, and a deficit in produce or other provision; مِنْ may identify what suffers the loss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To diminish or impair another person’s right or due; to deprive, shortchange, or defraud someone of part of it, and sometimes to deny or disacknowledge the right altogether.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A double-transitive construction in which the person and the affected right or due are both expressed or understood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attribute a defect or fault to someone; detract from their reputation, censure or reproach them, or impugn their character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use concerning criticism or disparagement of a person rather than the reduction of a material amount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask, demand, or seek a reduction or abatement in the price.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X commercial construction, especially of a buyer negotiating the price.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weakness of intellect, or weakness with respect to religion and intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person’s intellectual or religious condition as a specialized extension of deficiency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quantity that has gone or been lost from something that has been decreased or diminished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the amount of the loss itself, rather than merely the state or process of diminution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A defect, imperfection, fault, vice, or base quality that leads to deficiency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe a person’s quality, disposition, practice, habit, or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of attributing or imputing defect, fault, or vice to people; censuring, reproaching, or speaking against them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive use associated with the derived verbs for attributing defects or criticizing character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deficient or incomplete; specifically, deficient in weight when said of a coin or other weighed item.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The coin usage concerns an item lighter than the required weight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In grammar, an incomplete or non-attributive verb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical grammatical term opposed to تامٌّ, a complete verb.

cautions: The seven-occurrence Quranic verb group combines active and passive voice, imperfect and imperative inflections, under the normalized dictionary headword نَقَصَ; these are grammatical variants rather than separate public forms.
